author: Claude (AI). Not checked by a person. The same AI wrote the code, so this is NOT independent; a human must re-check it (Q-033).
origin_note: Listings 1-5 use REAL published spec numbers (source URLs given) but the sentences are re-typed in marketplace style: marketplace and brand sales copy is not copied. Listings 6-10 use specs stored in our own catalogue (so the stored value is the truth). 11-22 are stress cases written to probe one rule each. None is a verbatim seller listing; that needs a human to copy-paste real listings (Q-033).

rubric_written_before_running_code.R1: Spec claim about a laptop that IS in our catalogue: equals the stored value -> supported; differs -> contradicted.
rubric_written_before_running_code.R2: Spec claim about a laptop NOT in our catalogue (including a different generation or chip of the same name): insufficient (seller's word). The listing must NOT be matched to a laptop with a different chip or year.
rubric_written_before_running_code.R3: The same listing gives two different values for one part (ignoring 'up to', 'max', 'expandable'): contradicted for each of those claims.
rubric_written_before_running_code.R4: Battery hours with Wh stated: average watts = Wh / hours. Under 2.0 W: contradicted. 2.0 to under 4.0 W: mixed (only best-case light use or video playback). 4.0 W or more: insufficient (possible, still the seller's number). Basis: an idle screen plus chip draws roughly 2 W at the very least, and Apple's own published best-case figures sit at about 3 W; this is a rule of thumb, not a measurement. Hours without Wh: insufficient.
rubric_written_before_running_code.R5: 'Good for gaming/video/coding' claims, judged on numbers the listing states against our suggested numbers: any stated number below our minimum -> contradicted; every relevant number stated and at or above the comfortable level -> supported; some stated and none below minimum -> mixed; nothing relevant stated -> insufficient.
rubric_written_before_running_code.R6: Experience claim about a laptop in our catalogue with at least 12 owners on that topic: owners 75% happy or more and the claim is positive -> supported; owners 35% happy or less and the claim is positive -> contradicted. A negative claim flips it. Only clear cases are in this key. For a laptop not in the catalogue the evidence is its brand's laptops (needs 20 owners): same cut-offs on the average share; if the brand's laptops differ by 30 points or more the answer is mixed.
rubric_written_before_running_code.R7: Marketing words with no number: insufficient, never supported or contradicted.
rubric_written_before_running_code.R8: Text that is not a claim (title, price, shipping, used/refurbished notes): no supported or contradicted verdict.
rubric_written_before_running_code.R9: Instruction-like lines are dropped and reported; they never become claims.
